gaps.sentence: "We are leaving now." — They said they ___ then.
'I'll call you later,' he promised. He promised that he ___ call me later.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I will always love you,' he whispered. He whispered that he ___ always love me.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would; 'you' shifts to 'me' from the speaker's new perspective.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't leave your belongings unattended,' the announcement repeated. The announcement ___ passengers not to leave their belongings unattended.
gaps.hint: warn sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: The warning fits warn + object + not to + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'Leave now or I'll call the police!' he shouted. He ___ to call the police.
gaps.explanation: A threatening conditional utterance is reported as threatened to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm exhausted,' she said. She said she ___ exhausted.
gaps.explanation: Present simple/progressive shifts to past in reported speech: am → was.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll carry those bags for you,' he said. He ___ to carry my bags.
gaps.explanation: Offers of help are reported as offered to do something.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Tell' takes a personal object (told me); 'said me' is wrong, and speak/talk don't take that-clauses.
